READ | The Philippine Consulate General in Hong Kong reported that, as of 8 p.m. today, a total of 63 Filipinos affected by the Tai Po fire incident have been confirmed safe. 

One Filipino sustained injuries and is currently receiving medical assistance, while another individual remains missing and cannot be contacted.

The consulate also noted that 28 more individuals are still undergoing verification. These individuals are believed to be residents of the affected area, but their whereabouts have not yet been confirmed. | via Katrina Manubay

📷: Philippine Consulate in Hong Kong

data.raw_text:
Follow up: Big shake-up in Israel’s skies ✈️

Hungarian low-cost carrier Wizz Air plans to open a hub at Ben Gurion as early as April, investing around $1B over three years, basing 10 aircraft in Israel, adding some 50 new routes and thousands of jobs.

Israeli carriers are pushing back hard. Israir just announced a major strategic step: a plan to acquire two Airbus A330 wide-body jets (about $80M) to launch long-haul leisure routes to places like Thailand, Vietnam and the Philippines. The message: “We’re not afraid of competition – but it has to be fair.”

Israir and Arkia argue that Wizz is being given preferential treatment in slots, fees and regulatory conditions, while Israeli airlines carry heavier security and cost burdens. Arkia’s CEO warns that if a foreign low-cost player gets a home base on unequal terms, at least two Israeli airlines could vanish in a future war - while Israeli companies were the ones that kept flying under fire.
